MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  MARCH 27, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Kane Thuyen

  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

  City Clerk Heidi Luce

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 29-16: PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take public
  testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; and 4) Continue PA-29-16 to the next regular meeting
  of April 10, 2018.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and reviewed
  concerns raised in the correspondence received regarding this project including the
  correspondence placed on the dais.

  Carmelo Sorce, Director of Engineering, California Water Service Company reviewed a
  PowerPoint presentation and video providing further background and details concerning
  the project.

  Chad Brown, Design Builder, Black & Veatch reviewed a PowerPoint presentation
  providing further details concerning the design, construction, traffic control and
  timeline for the project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR HUFF called for public comment.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 27, 2018
   Carol Reinhart, 4339 Canyon View Lane (PVP) expressed concern regrading the
  operational noise from the pump house as well as the noise from the backup generator.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell regarding regular testing of the generator, Mr.
  Sorce commented that the generator will be tested monthly, during the day for 15
  minutes.

  Claire Donias, 280135 Sea Shell Way (RPV) expressed concern regarding the soil
  stability in the area.

  Steve Ferron, 4347 Canyon View Lane (PVP) expressed concern regarding a lack of
  communication with the Westfield Home Owners Association from Cal Water regarding
  the project. He further expressed concern regarding the location of the pump house, the
  operational noise from the pump house, the noise from the backup generator and the
  architectural design of the pump house.

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the architectural design and sound attenuating
  features of the pump house.

  Kit Fox, City Manager’s Office, City of Rancho Palos Verdes, commented that the Rancho
  Palos Verdes City Council has taken a position in support of the project. He further
  commented that RPV is appreciative of the efforts made thus far to address the concerns
  raised regarding traffic and noise impacts.

  Yongqiang Shi, 27292 Beechgate Drive (RPV) expressed concern regarding soil stability,
  specifically during a major seismic event; operational noise; and the impacts of ground
  vibration on slope stability.

  Eileen Hupp, Executive Director, Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce
  expressed the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce’s support for the project
  and its positive impact on water reliability on the Palos Verdes Peninsula.

  David Spiser, 4348 Canyon View Lane (PVP) expressed concern regarding the location
  and operational noise from the pump house.

  Bill Gerstner, 5317 Rolling Ridge Road (RPV) expressed concern regarding the
  thoroughness of the Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) specifically regarding traffic
  impacts, the waterline’s proximity to the landfill and possible leakage; and the ability to
  manage the existing watershed.

  Cory Watts, 27243 Eastvale Road (PVP) expressed concern regarding fire and suggested
  adding a fire hydrant.

  Doug Deecy, 27938 Beechgate Drive (RPV) agreed with the concerns raised regarding
  noise and soil stability; and expressed further concern regarding the effect that ongoing
  vibration may have on the slope.

  Meredith Bloss, Beechgate Drive (RPV) agreed with the concerns raised regarding noise
  and architectural features; and expressed further concern regarding soil stability
  pointing to a recent article featuring an Earthquake Hazard Zone Map.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 27, 2018
   Patty Humphrey, 14 Pony Lane expressed concern regarding a lack of communication
  pertaining to relocation of horses and the trail closures. She expressed further concern
  regarding the impact this project will have on the horses in the community.

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the communication plan for providing information
  to the equestrian community.

  Bruce Elmer Grimes, successor to “Farmer G” Grimes expressed appreciation for the
  fact that the “Farmer G” Tunnel will not be impacted by the project and further
  suggested that a horse facility be used as the architectural standard for the pump
  house.

  Carol Reinhart further commented regarding the aesthetics of the pump house and
  encouraged a Mediterranean, residential architectural style.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired as to the effect increased project costs will
  have on rates paid for water service.

  Mr. Sorce commented that Cal Water is committed to addressing the noise and aesthetic
  concerns raised while maintaining the functionality of the pump house. With regard to
  the generator, he commented that it will only be operated when absolutely necessary
  and it will be enclosed.

  Discussion ensued concerning addressing the noise issue.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF regarding the architectural design of the pump house, Mr.
  Sorce commented that Cal Water is open to entertaining other aesthetic features while
  maintaining functionality.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that this is a long-coming, necessary
  project and the City is committed to listening to the concerns raised by the entire
  Peninsula. He inquired as to the possibility of adding fire hydrants as part of the project.

  Mr. Sorce commented that currently, a fire hydrant is proposed in front of the pump
  house; but there is an opportunity to look at other locations for adding fire hydrants if
  there is a need and sufficient pressure.

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the public outreach associated with the project; the
  location of the pump house; and traffic impacts. COUNCILMEMER ZERUNYAN
  suggested that Cal Water further engage the Westfield residents.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, with regard to the issue raised
  regarding the landfill, Planning Director Wahba stated that the project does not go over
  the landfill and DTSC is recommending approval.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL regarding possible leaks in the pipeline,
  specifically in the area near the landfill, Mr. Sorce stated that pressures are monitored
  daily to assess whether or not there is a leak and physical monitoring is also done.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 27, 2018
   Further discussion ensued concerning the traffic impacts.  MAYOR PRO TEM
  MITCHELL suggested that there be a contingency plan related to traffic flow should
  there be a major accident one of the other routes while the roadway is closed during
  construction.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding the driveway access to the
  pump station, Planning Director Wahba stated that the matter has been addressed and
  the width of the roadway allows for deceleration prior to reaching the driveway without
  impacting traffic.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding trail closures, Planning
  Director Wahba stated that the trial closures will be clearly marked with detours noted.
  Mr. Sorce further commented that Cal Water is developing a detailed detour plan for the
  horse trail system.

  Following discussion, it was the concurrence of the CITY COUNCIL to request that Cal
  Water provide additional aesthetic options for the pump house including a
  Mediterranean design option and provide responses to the issues raised including noise,
  and continue this matter to the next City Council meeting.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING ON THIS MATTER
  TO THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING OF APRIL 10, 2018

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

  NONE.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 02-18: ORDINANCE NO. 721 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 17.43 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATED TO CANNABIS FACILITIES, CULTIVATION AND DELIVERIES

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct second reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 721.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CONDUCT SECOND READING AND ADOPT
  ORDINANCE NO. 721 AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 17.43 OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE RELATED TO CANNABIS
  FACILITIES, CULTIVATION AND DELIVERIES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 27, 2018
   Mayor Huff read Ordinance No. 721 by title only.

B.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH TRIPEPI SMITH FOR PUBLIC
  ENGAGEMENT SUPPORT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve: 1) the Professional Services Agreement
  with Tripepi Smith for monthly service in an amount of $4,294.58 per month for a six-
  month period; and 2) the Professional Services Agreement with Tripepi Smith for special
  projects in the amount of $34,972.50 to be completed in fiscal years 2017-18, 2018-19
  an2019-20 for support in implementing public engagement and outreach strategies.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to MAYOR HUFF, Assistant to the City Manager Davis commented that the
  tasks associated with the City’s current agreement with Tripepi Smith have been
  substantially completed and the new agreement is for additional services to be provided
  as shown in the scope of work.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  confirmed that the City can cancel the agreement at any time with 30-days’ notice.

  MAYOR HUFF commented that to her it seems that staff, with some training from Tripepi
  Smith could ultimately do many of the tasks at a lower cost.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that it may be a good idea to contract with
  a firm that has expertise in this area.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL suggested moving forward since community engagement
  was identified as a priority.

  With regard to the concerns raised City Manager Prichard suggested that language could
  be added to the effect that special projects in future years will not go forward without
  written authorization from the City.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the City has had a very good
  relationship with Ryder Smith and any issues that may arise will be addressed
  accordingly.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE TWO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENTS WITH TRIPEPI SMITH FOR: 1) MONTHLY SERVICE IN AN
  AMOUNT OF $4,294.58 PER MONTH FOR A SIX-MONTH PERIOD; AND 2)
  SPECIAL PROJECTS IN THE AMOUNT OF $34,972.50 TO BE
  COMPLETED IN FISCAL YEARS 2017-18, 2018-19 AND 2019-20 FOR
  SUPPORT IN IMPLEMENTING PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT AND OUTREACH
  STRATEGIES WITH AMENDED LANGUAGE REGARDING FUTURE
  SPECIAL PROJECTS INCLUDED SUBJECT TO THE CITY’S ATTORNEY’S
  APPROVAL.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
MARCH 27, 2018
   AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  RESOLUTIONS NO. 2418 AND NO. 2419 ESTABLISHING ADMINISTRATIVE ANALYST
  AND CODE COMPLIANCE OFFICER JOB CLASSIFICATIONS, DESCRIPTIONS AND
  RESPECTIVE SALARY RANGES WITHIN THE PROFESSIONAL EMPLOYEE GROUP

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolutions No. 2418 and No. 2419

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material). She
  noted that the work schedule for the Code Compliance Officer position will need a slight
  amendment to reflect a 10/80 work schedule.

  MAYOR HUFF expressed concern regarding the pension obligations associated with
  adding full-time positions.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that this is a part of succession planning and
  it is likely that pension obligations will be reduced as long-term employees retire.

  In response MAYOR HUFF regarding the reasoning for full-time vs. part-time positons,
  City Manager Prichard stated with regard to the Code Compliance Officer position, case
  management efficiency, responsiveness to the public are increased with a full-time
  position and the cost of utilizing City Prosecutor are typically decreased as experience
  is gained. With regard to the Administrative Analyst positon, he stated that adding this
  positon will allow specific focus on public safety related matters while allowing the
  Assistant to the City Manager to focus on the primary duties of that position.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2418 ESTABLISHING AN
  ADMINISTRATIVE ANALYST OFFICER JOB CLASSIFICATION, DESCRIPTION
  AND RESPECTIVE SALARY RANGE WITHIN THE PROFESSIONAL EMPLOYEE
